body:
AMEND — the proposed graph is acyclic, but one wording change is needed to preserve the accepted B0-A closure contract without a false unblock.

The accepted V2 says B0 closes after A-D have accepted outcomes AND all named owner actions have explicit dispositions; the architectural decision keeps the owner-only rights/access decisions open. The proposal correctly makes only Sherlock-or-an-actually-ratified-replacement the favorable source outcome. It should not require favorable pyannote, MF2, FilmFestival, or future-corpus decisions when those leaves are not selected. But “not selected” must itself be an explicit, reviewed disposition such as NotSelected/ExcludedUntilSelected, with no admission implied. Silence or an absent row is not a disposition.

Tracker shape:

- Create the bounded Sherlock-or-ratified-replacement bead; do not try to depend on one row inside the broader owner-action bead, because Mote dependencies are bead-granular.
- Make the aggregate B0 bead depend on B0-A, B0-C, B0-D, and the already-closed B0-B bead. The closed B0-B edge is useful traceability even though it adds no live blocker. I independently confirmed f203b783 is an ancestor of current main.
- Make future C1 depend on aggregate B0 and P1 separately.
- Do not make aggregate B0 depend on C1, D0, or the whole broader owner-action registry. Optional owner actions become dependencies only for a vertical that selects those leaves.

That yields the directed gate A/C/D/B -> B0 -> C1, with P1 -> C1 separately; no edge returns from C1 or D0, so no cycle. It also prevents the two false states: optional future work holding the provider-free substrate, or an empty/partial owner-action table unlocking it.

ACCEPT if “B0-A accepted outcome” includes a reviewed scope/disposition record accounting for every named owner-action leaf, including explicit NotSelected outcomes. Otherwise AMEND as above. No files, beads, source access, or implementation are authorized by this review.
